telemetry_findings.title: backfill_run_days.calendar_events_considered is 0 for every EXECUTE day although discovery examined calendar events
telemetry_findings.evidence_query: SELECT sum(calendar_events_considered) FROM backfill_run_days WHERE backfill_run_id=... -> 0; SELECT sum(calendar_events_found) FROM lecture_discovery_runs over the same window -> 239
telemetry_findings.detail: 239 calendar events were examined across 22 discovery runs, and every EXECUTE day recorded 0. app/orchestration/backfill.py:_record builds its default day_counts with a hardcoded 'calendar_events_considered': 0, and _counts_from never reads calendar_events_found from the orchestrator summary. The PREVIEW path (_preview_day) does populate it, which is why only EXECUTE runs look empty. No lecture data is affected.
telemetry_findings.recommended_fix: Have _counts_from carry calendar_events_found out of summary['discovery'] the way _preview_day already does, and pass it to _record as day_counts.

telemetry_findings.title: The 'suppressed' counter does not count duplicate suppressions
telemetry_findings.evidence_query: SELECT action FROM lecture_pipeline_run_items WHERE action LIKE '%SUPPRESS_DUPLICATE_EVENT%' vs SELECT business_date, suppressed FROM backfill_run_days
telemetry_findings.detail: backfill_run_days reports suppressed on the days ['2026-09-02'], but SUPPRESS_DUPLICATE_EVENT actually executed on ['2026-09-04', '2026-09-11']. app/orchestration/backfill.py:_counts_from maps 'suppressed' to counts['skipped_count'], and _counts() in the orchestrator uses skipped_count as its RESIDUAL bucket - anything not failed, not review, not waiting and not settled at NOTHING_TO_DO. A genuinely suppressed duplicate settles at NOTHING_TO_DO and is therefore counted as COMPLETE, while unsettled lectures are reported to the operator as 'suppressed'. The two numbers coincided at 2 by chance.
telemetry_findings.recommended_fix: Count SUPPRESS_DUPLICATE_EVENT actions (or duplicate_suppression annotations) for the suppressed counter, and surface skipped_count under a name that says what it is, e.g. 'unsettled'.

telemetry_findings.title: 'already complete' counts lectures complete AFTER the run, not before
telemetry_findings.evidence_query: backfill_run_days for 2026-09-02: newly_discovered=8, already_complete=5, matched=8 - all eight lectures were created by this run, so none can have been complete beforehand
telemetry_findings.detail: _counts_from maps already_complete to counts['completed_count'], which _counts() derives from the state at the END of the cycle. The label reads as 'was already done', which for a day of newly discovered lectures is impossible and misleading.
telemetry_findings.recommended_fix: Rename to complete_at_end_of_day, or compute a true before-count from the pre-run state snapshot.

findings.title: Lectures finished the backfill without reaching a settled state
findings.evidence_query: SELECT lecture_id, final_state FROM lecture_pipeline_run_items WHERE status='SUCCEEDED' AND final_state <> 'NOTHING_TO_DO'
findings.recommended_fix: Re-run these lectures through the normal orchestrator (RETRY). Confirm current state first - the resolver may already report them settled if a later cycle finished them.

findings.title: A lecture is neither complete, waiting, suppressed nor in review, and the resolver offers no reason
findings.recommended_fix: RETRY through the orchestrator; investigate the blocking stage first.

findings.title: Lectures whose QA is finished carry a stage the resolver reports STALE
findings.evidence_query: PipelineStateResolver.for_lecture -> a STALE stage with a named reason while QA_EVALUATION and QA_RENDER are COMPLETE
findings.recommended_fix: Decide deliberately rather than reflexively re-running. SELECT_TRANSCRIPT would re-stale everything downstream and could turn settled compatibility rows into WOULD_UPDATE decisions that need an operator. The QA answers are not wrong; only the lineage marker is behind the transcript content.

findings.title: Cue start times are not monotonic by cue_index
findings.evidence_query: SELECT d.document_id, d.lecture_id FROM public.lecture_transcript_documents d JOIN public.lecture_sessions l ON l.lecture_id=d.lecture_id WHERE l.session_date BETWEEN %s AND %s AND EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM ( SELECT start_ms, lag(start_ms) OVER (ORDER BY cue_index) prev FROM public.lecture_transcript_cues WHERE document_id=d.document_id) t WHERE t.prev IS NOT NULL AND t.start_ms < t.prev)
findings.recommended_fix: None. Overlapping speech is real; the parser already records it as overlapping_cue_count and marks the document PARSED_WITH_WARNINGS.

findings.title: A finalized QA evaluation rests on an EMPTY attendance snapshot
findings.evidence_query: attendance snapshot source_row_count=0 AND effective_member_count=0 AND qa_status IN ('COMPLETED','NON_DELIVERED')
findings.detail: 2026-09-17 Martech - Thur met=11/11, engagement=0.00%; 2026-09-17 G2 -  Keith - Strategy and Planning - June 2026 met=11/11, engagement=0.00%
findings.recommended_fix: Do not repair by hand. These evaluations were produced before the attendance-required policy; the resolver now reports the lectures WAITING and refuses to advance them. Recover attendance, then let the normal pipeline supersede the evaluation.

findings.title: A rendered lecture has no legacy compatibility row and none is protected
findings.evidence_query: PipelineStateResolver LEGACY_QA_SYNC state in (MISSING, STALE) while QA_RENDER is COMPLETE
findings.detail: Downstream consumers (positive-clips producer, dashboard) cannot see these lectures.
findings.recommended_fix: Run SYNC_LEGACY_QA through the orchestrator (RETRY). Do not write the row by hand.

findings.title: A pre-existing n8n row occupies the session_id a coded lecture would use
findings.evidence_query: rendered session_id EXISTS in qa_doctors_sessions with no lecture_qa_legacy_writes ownership row
findings.detail: This is the ownership model working as designed: the writer returns PROTECTED_EXISTING_LEGACY_ROW and the stage reports NOT_APPLICABLE rather than asking anyone to overwrite history.
findings.recommended_fix: None. Do not overwrite. If the coded answer must supersede n8n's, that is an explicit operator decision.

findings.title: Perfect eligibility computed under a superseded version
findings.recommended_fix: Re-run EVALUATE_PERFECT; the resolver already treats these as not-current.

findings.title: A published Perfect Lecture row is no longer eligible under the current policy and has not been retracted
findings.evidence_query: qa_perfect_lectures JOIN lecture_perfect_lecture_legacy_writes JOIN lecture_perfect_lecture_results (version=kbc_perfect_v2_attendance_required) WHERE is_perfect IS FALSE
findings.detail: 2026-09-17 Martech - Thur -> PENDING_ATTENDANCE_DATA (published with engagement=0.00%, attended=0)
findings.recommended_fix: Operator decision, not an automated one. At least one was published on an EMPTY attendance snapshot and is visible to downstream consumers as a Perfect Lecture with 0 attendees; treat that as the priority. Retracting a published Perfect row has outward consequences because the Excel Sync workflow may already have exported it.
